# DRM ground-truth fixtures

These fixtures let the Rust/WASM DRM decoder be verified without a live shortwave
DRM broadcast (which is not reliably receivable on a SAN-90 in a lab).

## `drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32` + `manifest.json`

A synthesised DRM30 signal with **known** content: robustness mode B, spectrum
occupancy 3 (10 kHz), 64-QAM SM MSC, 16-QAM SDC, long interleaving, EEP protection
level 1. The SDC carries a station label `SAN90 DRM TEST` and an AAC (24 kHz SBR
mono) audio service; the FAC carries service id `0x123456`, one audio service, no
data services. Full ground truth lives in `manifest.json`.

- `drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32` — interleaved I/Q `float32` (little-endian), 48 kHz
  complex, 6.0 s (288000 complex samples).
- `manifest.json` — format, signal/FAC/SDC/MSC ground truth, and the generator's
  self-check result.

## `drm_modeB_so{0,5}_48k_xhe.f32` — DRM30 FAC-selected occupancy

Two 6-second, 48 kHz complex float IQ signals generated by DecDRM v0.5.1 `decdrm tx`
using the bench station settings with mode B and occupancies SO0 (4.5 kHz) / SO5
(20 kHz). The transmitter writes int16 stereo I/Q WAV, converted to interleaved
little-endian float32 I/Q with `ffmpeg -f f32le -acodec pcm_f32le`. Both carry one
xHE-AAC tone service (`SAN90 DRM BENCH`), MSC 64-QAM, SDC 16-QAM, long
interleaving and EEP 0/1. Source code from the GPL transmitter is not included.

`wasm/tests/drm_occupancy.rs` feeds both in one buffer and worker-sized blocks,
asserting that the FAC selects SO0/SO5 (instead of the initial SO3 map), SDC/MSC
and audio access units decode, and both feeding patterns return identical bits.
The separate mode A/C/D SO3 fixtures remain the regression for those modes.

## `drm_modeE_so0_96k_aac.f32` — synthetic DRM+ mode E chain fixture

This is a deterministic, zero-noise 96 kHz mode E signal generated by the in-tree Rust test
`wasm/src/digital/drm/mod.rs::mode_e_acquires_and_demodulates_a_synthetic_signal`. It carries
spec-shaped mode E FAC (116-bit, rate 1/4, four-frame identity/toggle), a valid 4-QAM SDC
block describing one 24 kHz AAC service, and four-frame MSC content. The native test checks
FAC/SDC CRCs, depth-6 MSC decoding bit-for-bit, and the paired 200 ms AAC logical frames;
`frontend/src/__tests__/drmPlusAudio.test.ts` checks the same fixture through the shipped wasm
ABI at both 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz sound-card output rates.

This fixture verifies the implemented DRM+ chain independently of a transmitter. It is not an
off-air VHF recording and does not replace real DRM+ propagation, frequency-offset, or
reconfiguration validation. The test can regenerate it with:

```sh
cd wasm
WEBSA_DRM_MODE_E_FIXTURE=../tests/fixtures/drm/drm_modeE_so0_96k_aac.f32 \
  cargo test --lib digital::drm::tests::mode_e_acquires_and_demodulates_a_synthetic_signal
```

## Provenance and licence

The DRM30 transmitter fixtures (including SO0/SO3/SO5) are **data** emitted by running
DecDRM. The mode E fixture above is generated by this repository's own Rust test, not DecDRM:

- Project: https://github.com/CasualArclamp/DecDRM (v0.5.1, commit
  `b1fbd87f3d3e4709ff838d5120724fb4506253f6`), licence **GPL-2.0-or-later**.
- Generator: `crates/decdrm-core/examples/gen_fixture.rs` for the original mode B SO3
  fixture. The SO0/SO5 fixtures use `decdrm tx` with the station configuration in
  `tools/bench/drm_bench/station_iq.toml` copied to a temporary file and `occupancy` set to
  0 or 5; the int16 IQ WAV output is converted to f32 IQ with `ffmpeg`.

The I/Q samples describe a signal defined by the ETSI ES 201 980 standard and are
not GPL source; only the *generator tool* is GPL. DecDRM is therefore kept out of
this repository and used solely as an external fixture generator / oracle — the
in-tree Rust/WASM decoder is an independent implementation.

## `aac_sine_24k.{drm,ga,json}` — DRM AAC audio fixture

A run of 9 re-serialised DRM AAC access units plus their original MPEG-4 GA
access units, used to verify the **audio** stage of the DRM receive chain
(MSC → AAC access units → PCM) independently of the OFDM/FAC/SDC stages.

- `aac_sine_24k.drm` — 9 DRM AAC access units (36 bytes each), concatenated:
  the GA frames re-serialised to DRM syntax (VCB11 section data, HCR spectral
  data, `aac_crc_bits`).
- `aac_sine_24k.ga` — the original 9 GA AAC-LC access units (320 bytes each),
  the lossless reference.
- `aac_sine_24k.json` — frame sizes, codec config, and the verification result.

The signal is a 1 kHz sine, AAC-LC 24 kHz mono, 64 kbit/s CBR, 960-sample
frames (the DRM transform length). Generated by `tools/fixtures/gen_drm_aac_fixture.py`
from FDK-AAC (960-sample encoder patch) GA frames re-serialised by
`tools/fixtures/drm_aac_reserialize.py`. Verify with `tools/fixtures/verify_drm_aac.c`:

```sh
cc -O2 -I <fdk>/libAACdec/include -I <fdk>/libSYS/include \
   -I <fdk>/libMpegTPDec/include -I <fdk>/libFDK/include \
   -I <fdk>/libSBRdec/include -I <fdk>/libSACdec/include \
   -I <fdk>/libPCMutils/include -I <fdk>/libArithCoding/include \
   -I <fdk>/libDRCdec/include \
   tools/fixtures/verify_drm_aac.c <fdk>/build/libfdk-aac.a -lm -o verify_drm_aac
./verify_drm_aac tests/fixtures/drm/aac_sine_24k.drm \
                  tests/fixtures/drm/aac_sine_24k.ga 36 320
# 9 frames: mismatch=0 energy=139955180 -> OK
```

The DRM decode matches the GA decode bit-for-bit (`mismatch=0`) and is
non-silent — the re-serialiser is lossless. (The decoder has a two-frame
priming delay, so the first two decoded frames are silent; the assertion
totals energy across all 9.)

## `drm_modeB_so3_48k_aac.f32` — end-to-end audio fixture

Identical to the main fixture (Mode B / SO3, 10 kHz, 64-QAM SM MSC, 16-QAM SDC,
long interleaving), except the MSC payload is a **real 24 kHz AAC audio super
frame** (10 re-serialised DRM AAC access units of a 1 kHz sine) instead of the
xorshift bit stream. This exercises the full receive chain through to PCM:
`DrmReceiver → deframe_audio → decode_audio → audio_pcm`, asserted non-silent by
`wasm/tests/drm_fixture.rs::fixture_deframes_real_aac_audio` (native deframe) and
`frontend/src/__tests__/drmAudioEndToEnd.test.ts` (wasm32 AAC decode through the
`websa_dsp_drm_audio_pcm` ABI).

Generated by the DecDRM `gen_fixture.rs` example with its MSC payload replaced by
`tools/fixtures/gen_drm_aac_fixture.py` + the DRM AAC re-serialiser; see the example's
comments and `tools/fixtures/drm_aac_reserialize.py`.

## `drm_live_modeB_so3_48828.f32` + `live_manifest.json` — live bench capture

The baseband the browser DSP worker receives from the bench loop (DecDRM transmitter →
PlutoSDR → radiated 2 m → SAN-90 external antenna). It is the decoder's exact input: the
IQBF payload of the `?iq=1` WebSocket, captured with `tools/bench/drm_capture.py`.

Unlike the synthesised fixtures, this file keeps the three properties of a live link:

- the channelizer's rate (48828.125 Hz published, 48833.85 Hz measured), not 48 kHz;
- an arbitrary start point in the transmission super frame;
- real level (rms +15.6 dBFS, about 30x full scale), noise and channel conditions.

Dream, the external decoder, decodes this file: snr 21.0 dB, robustness mode B, 10 kHz,
FAC/SDC/MSC status 0, service label `SAN90 DRM BENCH`, 20.96 kbit/s. The bench signal is
therefore good, and the receiver under test is the failing part. The file is 6 s of the
10 s capture.

- `drm_live_modeB_so3_48828.f32` — interleaved I/Q `float32` (little-endian), 6 s, 287999
  complex samples at the published rate.
- `live_manifest.json` — bench settings, measured rates and level, the oracle result, and
  the provenance of the transmitter configuration.

Regression tests: `wasm/tests/drm_live_fixture.rs` (the live capture must decode) and
`wasm/tests/drm_phy_robustness.rs` (the synthesised fixture must survive 15 dB SNR, a
200 us echo and the bench level). Reproduce the session with `docs/en/DRM_BENCH.md`.

## Regenerating

Clone DecDRM (outside this repo), drop in the `gen_fixture.rs` example, and run:

```sh
cargo build --release -p decdrm-core --example gen_fixture
./target/release/examples/gen_fixture B 3 6.0 tests/fixtures/drm/drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32
```

Then paste the printed summary back into `manifest.json`'s `self_check` block if it
changed. The parameters are `gen_fixture <mode A-D> <so 0-5> <seconds> <out.f32>`.

## Real off-air recordings

For later validation against real broadcasts, the DecDRM test suite references a set
of off-air DRM recordings (e.g. `DW_ModeB_10kHz.flac`, `RTL_ModeB_10kHz.flac`,
`Deutschlandradio_ModeA_10kHz.flac`) with known mode/occupancy; see
`crates/decdrm-core/tests/recordings.rs` in DecDRM. Those recordings are not
committed there and are intentionally out of scope for the committed fixture set.
